jobs.employer_name: Siemens Energy Global GmbH & Co. KG
jobs.description: A Snapshot of Your Day This role puts you at the financial center of the carve-out. On 25 August 2026 Siemens Energy announced preparations for the legal and operational separation of Transformation of Industry into a standalone company, a fast-growing business with around 17,000 employees, €6 billion of revenue and a double-digit profit margin. A separation of this scale needs one integrated financial view of what it costs — and you are the person who creates it, working directly with the Carve-out Program Lead and the individual carve-out workstreams.Your day starts with a review of the latest carve-out cost forecast. One workstream has revised its implementation plan, another needs a decision on cost allocation, and the program lead needs a consolidated financial view for the next steering meeting. You bring the information together, challenge assumptions and translate developments into a clear management perspective. Later, you work with Finance, IT, HR, Legal and other workstreams to clarify financial impacts and prepare recommendations. Priorities can shift quickly and not every structure is defined yet; your contribution is transparency, financial discipline and well-founded decisions.This is a rare moment to join. A new company is being built, and with it a new Finance organization: the central Business Controlling team of Transformation of Industry is developing into the Corporate FP&A department of that company, an organization of more than 100 finance professionals. The role also has a clear next step built in: once the carve-out is completed, you move into TI Performance or Function Controlling and apply everything you have learned about the business to its ongoing performance steering.How You’ll Make an Impact * Act as the central finance business partner for the Carve-out Program Lead and workstreams, providing financial guidance for separation and standalone-readiness decisions through business cases, scenario analyses and financial assessments* Establish an integrated view of carve-out costs, including commitments, actuals, budgets and forecasts, and coordinate planning, steering and reporting across workstreams, entities and functions* Challenge cost assumptions, identify deviations and risks early, and drive corrective actions to ensure effective financial steering* Develop transparent charging and allocation concepts for carve-out costs in collaboration with Accounting, Tax, Legal and relevant Finance teams* Prepare concise management reports and decision papers for program leadership, Finance leadership and governance bodies, ensuring consistent definitions, controls and audit trails while leveraging digital solutions to reduce manual effort and improve data quality* Transition into TI Performance or Function Controlling after the carve-out, bringing business knowledge into ongoing performance steeringWhat You Bring* A university degree in Finance, Business Administration, Economics, Industrial Engineering or a related field* Longstanding experience in controlling, FP&A, finance business partnering, project controlling or transformation finance; experience with carve-outs, separations or large transformation programs is a plus* A strong command of budgeting, forecasting, cost controlling, management reporting and variance analysis, with the ability to structure ambiguous topics, connect multiple data sources and turn financial information into practical recommendations* A hands-on mindset and the resilience to deliver under high workload, changing priorities and incomplete information* Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, including the confidence to challenge constructively across functions and seniority levels, combined with advanced Excel and PowerPoint skills; experience with SAP, Power BI, SAC or comparable tools is a plus* Fluent English; additional languages are an asset but not required About the TeamOur Transformation of Industry division is decarbonizing the industrial sector. Increasing electrification and efficiency are key and demand for green H2 and derivative fuels will rise. We enable decarbonization of the industrial sector and the transition to sustainable processes, building on a strong industrial customer base, a global network, diverse technologies, and integrated execution capabilities.Who is Siemens Energy? At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With ~100.000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. The technologies created in our research departments and factories drive the energy transition and provide the base for one sixth of the world's electricity generation.Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation.      Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Energy: https://www.siemens-energy.com/employeevideoOur Commitment to Diversity Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by over 130 nationalities. Siemens Energy celebrates character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences. Rewards/Benefits * In addition to an attractive remuneration package in line with the market, you can expect an attractive employer-financed company pension scheme* We also offer the opportunity to become a Siemens Energy shareholder* We offer our employees the opportunity to work flexibly and remotely, and our inspiring offices provide space for collaboration and creativity* The professional and personal development of our employees is very important to us. We provide them with the opportunities to learn and develop in a self-determined way, various attractive programmes and learning materials are available for this purpose* In relation to the "compatibility of family and work", we have a wide range of offers, e.g. flexible working time models, childcare places at many locations, the possibility of trial part-time work or even a sabbatical  We value equal opportunities and welcome applications from people with disabilities.You do not need to tick every box. If this role excites you and you bring most of it, we would like to hear from you.https://jobs.siemens-energy.com/jobs

jobs.occupation: Failure Analysis Engineer, Electrical (m/w/d) Berlin, Germany (Qualitätsingenieur/in)
jobs.description: What to ExpectWe are looking for a Failure Analysis Engineer, Electrical, to join the failure analysis team in Berlin (Tesla Engineering Germany). This is an individual contributor role. You report to the mechanical failure analysis lead. The team finds root cause and contributing factors, so Tesla can reduce field, production, and development issues. You work with design, manufacturing, quality, and other engineering teams, across vehicle and energy products, including current models and products still in development. We need an electrical engineer with industry experience, not a new graduate, to identify and characterize electrical failures. You use a multimeter, an oscilloscope, and other basic electrical test equipment to confirm the symptom, isolate the fault, and support root cause with Design, Manufacturing, and Quality. The right person is comfortable on the bench: probing boards, reading a schematic well enough to troubleshoot, and explaining what they found. Manufacturing experience is a strong plus. That includes production test, yield, process, or factory debug.?What You’ll Do- Debug and troubleshoot analog and digital systems with a digital multimeter, oscilloscope, power supply, and related bench equipment. - Confirm and recreate failures seen in engineering, production, and the field. - Drive root cause from the first report toward a countermeasure, with the original design engineers and the other failure analysis engineers. - Use the analytical tools the case needs, including functional test, electrical debug, and X-ray. - Design experiments to test a theory, and run them yourself or with the technician. - Document findings and investigation status. Report root cause and the relevant facts to engineering and manufacturing. - Bring prior failure experience into design reviews and DFMEAs. - Partner with manufacturing on production and yield-related electrical issues that come into the lab.?What You’ll Bring- Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or equivalent experience. - 1-3 years of industry experience in electrical debug, test, manufacturing, or a related hands-on role. This is not a new-graduate role. Internships and coursework alone are not enough. - Hands-on use of a digital multimeter and an oscilloscope, and experience with power supplies and other common electrical test equipment. - Able to read a schematic and troubleshoot analog and digital circuitry at a basic to intermediate level. - Strong written and spoken English. - Self-driven, structured, and comfortable in a fast-paced lab. - Preferred: experience with common failure analysis techniques. - Preferred: manufacturing experience (production test, yield debug, process engineering, or factory electrical troubleshooting). - Preferred: soldering and rework on PCBAs. - Preferred: familiarity with common digital protocols (I2C, CAN, LIN).?Tesla is an Equal Opportunity / Affirmative Action employer committed to diversity in the workplace. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, age, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, gender identity or any other factor protected by applicable federal, state or local laws.Tesla is also committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. jobs.occupation: Lead Failure Analysis Engineer, Mechanical / Mechatronics (m/w/d) Berlin, Germany (Qualitätsingenieur/in)
jobs.description: What to ExpectWe are looking for a Failure Analysis Engineer to lead the failure analysis team in Berlin (Tesla Engineering Germany). This is the team lead. The electrical failure analysis engineer and the failure analysis technician report to you. The team finds root cause and contributing factors, so Tesla can reduce field, production, and development issues. You work with design, manufacturing, quality, and other engineering teams, across vehicle and energy products, including current models and products still in development. The role is hands-on. You own electromechanical failure analysis yourself, and you run the lab. You confirm and recreate failures, lead teardowns, and use optical microscopy, X-ray, and mechanical sample preparation to identify failure mechanisms. You report root cause and propose countermeasures with Design, Manufacturing, Quality, and the other failure analysis engineers. The right person has several years of industry experience, is comfortable taking assemblies apart and putting them back together, and can connect what they see under a microscope or on an X-ray to how the part was designed and built. A materials science background is preferred.?What You’ll Do- Lead the failure analysis team and laboratory. Manage operations, lab workflows, equipment, and the two people who report to you: the electrical failure analysis engineer and the failure analysis technician. - Drive failure analysis of electromechanical assemblies from the first report through root cause and countermeasure, including failure confirmation, recreation, and teardown inspection. - Use optical microscopes, 2D X-ray, and related inspection tools to characterize defects in mechanical and electromechanical hardware. - Prepare mechanical samples (sectioning, grinding, polishing) so failure interfaces can be inspected, and document what you find. - Disassemble and reassemble electromechanical assemblies while keeping the original form and function. - Design and run experiments to test a hypothesis, either yourself or with the technician. - Document inspections, replication tests, and teardowns in written reports, images, and the project tracking system. - Work with Design, Manufacturing, Quality, and suppliers on containment and corrective action. - Bring prior failure experience into design reviews and DFMEAs.?What You’ll Bring- Bachelor's or Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Materials Science, or equivalent experience. A materials science background is preferred. - 3-5 years of industry experience in failure analysis, reliability, product development, or a related hands-on engineering role. This is not a new-graduate role. - Hands-on experience with optical microscopes, X-ray inspection, and teardown of mechanical or electromechanical assemblies. - Able to take an assembly down to its subcomponents and explain what the parts are and how they work. - Able to fully disassemble and reassemble electromechanical assemblies without losing function or form. - Experience with mechanical sample preparation (saws, grinders, polishers) and with clear documentation: photos, optical images, and written reports. - Strong written and spoken English. Able to explain a failure mechanism clearly to design and manufacturing stakeholders. - Self-driven, structured, and comfortable in a fast-paced lab. - Preferred: tensile test, pressure or leak test, machine shop equipment, CAN or LIN, and oscilloscope.?Tesla is an Equal Opportunity / Affirmative Action employer committed to diversity in the workplace.
